even so: introduces something that is true in spite of what you have just said
typical: spoken and informal writing, at the start of a sentence or after 'but'. NOT for: 'even though' before a clause or 'even if' for imagined situations.
The test was difficult. Even so, most students passed.
He apologised. Even so, she was still angry.
The hotel had no sea view, but even so we enjoyed the stay.
